title: Svartsengi (Sundhnúkur crater row) eruption 16 Jul-5 Aug 2025: SIMULATED fire-fountain heights by fissure segment
centroid_method: IMO radar onset location 63.90N 22.35W shifted 0.85 km NNE for northward growth of the main fissure to 2.4 km; parallel 500 m fissure excluded; approx. +/-0.01 deg
source: Rhodes et al. (2026) Bull. Volcanol. 88:89, doi:10.1007/s00445-026-02006-3; supplement ESM2
model: model: h(t) = Hmax_seg * (1-exp(-B t)) exp(-C t) / peak, t = seconds since segment opening; rise-decay form of Rhodes et al. (2026) Eq. 2 | B = 0.03806 s^-1, C = 1.0680e-04 s^-1 (refit of Eq. 2 to all 37 segments of the four measured eruptions pooled; A = 0.677); curve peak at 2.6 min after opening | scaled so each segment peaks at its Hmax_seg (the pulse maximum). The fitted mean trend is A x these values. Model calibrated only on the first ~3 h of fountaining; later values are extrapolation. | eruption Hmax = 100 m (first segment), weighted mean of two regressions on the four measured eruptions (Dec 2023 93 m, Jan 2024 56 m, Mar 2024 124 m, Aug 2024 133 m): | H = -56.4 + 58.3 log10(Q_peak) [resid SD 15 m] -> 106 m with Q = 600 m3/s (~600 m3/s peak effusion assumed: lava area at ~8 h (3.2 km2) about half that of Nov 2024 at ~7 h (~7 km2), scaled from Nov 2024 1300 m3/s) | H = 46.6 + 18.6 L_fissure_km [resid SD 28 m] -> 91 m with L = 2.4 km | later segments: Hmax_seg = ratio x eruption Hmax, ratio = median of observed (segment max / eruption max) for segments opening <30 min (0.45), 30-120 min (0.39), >120 min (0.14) after onset (Rhodes et al. supplement)

segments.name: main_initial
segments.basis: initial 700-1000 m fissure; last crater active until early 5 Aug (IMO)

segments.name: main_north
segments.basis: northward opening reported at 05:05; main fissure 2.4 km by noon; northernmost crater ceased ~22:00 21 Jul (IMO)

segments.name: parallel
segments.basis: ~500 m second fissure open by noon; opening set to mid-window; activity confined to central main fissure by 11:30 18 Jul (IMO)
